Research/2025-26/Radio transients

Radio transients

V-SPARC: Detecting Long-Period Transients with VLITE

A search of archival low-frequency radio observations for rare sources that pulse on minute-to-hour timescales.

Research question

What did the project ask?

Can archival VLITE radio observations reveal new long-period transients and constrain how much sky coverage future searches require?

Significance

Why does it matter?

Only a small population of long-period transients is known, leaving their abundance and physical origin poorly constrained.

Method

What did the team do?

The team filtered VLITE configuration catalogs by signal-to-noise, compactness, catalog separation, and artifact indicators; inspected FITS images; cross-matched radio catalogs; recovered known transients as validation; and estimated fluence limits and areal burst density.

Principal result

What did the evidence show?

No new long-period transient was confirmed. The search recovered known detections and estimated a bright-burst density near one per 100,000 square degrees of suitable survey coverage.

Collaboration

Project-specific support

The project was conducted with Dr. Emil Polisensky of the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory.
